items.title: Jensen Huang Is Too Big to Fail - The Atlantic
items.summary: Huang, who founded Nvidia in 1993, is the company’s key figure, praised by many in the tech industry as one of the visionaries responsible for the rapid acceleration of artificial intelligence. He’s instrumental in the company’s engineering decisions, its allocation of chips, and other investments. He also has no clear successor. Outside of Silicon Valley, Huang has become a trusted adviser and ally to Trump on AI policy. Huang’s thinking on issues such as AI doomerism (he’s anti-doom) and chip [...] It is curious, then, that, as news came out that the Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang, had had a romantic relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who was also an asset of Beijing’s Ministry of State Security, notable factions of Silicon Valley and Washington, D.C., seemed nonplussed. “Even incredible humans make mistakes,” Bill Ackman, the billionaire hedge-fund manager, posted on X yesterday. “We should all support him and his family. Onward.” The venture capitalist Shaun Maguire offered a [...] citizens are all tied up in one progressively intricate technological and financial bet. In this way, Huang is the AI boom personified, a hyperobject of a man who has wound his way into the center of the economy and whose influence, depending on how you look at it, may usher in either prosperity or untold doom.

items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang faces scrutiny over alleged affair with Chinese spy | PBS News
items.summary:
Lawmakers, investors and tech leaders are assessing bombshell revelations about Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang. Huang admitted to an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. Nvidia designs chips and processors that power artificial intelligence and underpin much of the enormous investment in the industry. William Brangham reports.

## Read the Full Transcript

Notice: Transcripts are machine and human generated and lightly edited for accuracy. They may contain errors. [...] William Brangham:

The head of one of the companies' most critical to the development of artificial intelligence, Jensen Huang, admitted to having an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese tech executive and suspected spy in the pink dress. There's no relation. [...] Guo Jiakun, Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson (through interpreter):

We have previously responded to this matter. The so-called claims of a Chinese spy narrative are purely a groundless accusation.

William Brangham:

Jensen Huang, in a statement yesterday, admitted to the affair in a company-wide statement -- quote -- "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

items.title: The Good News About Jensen Huang’s Affair
items.summary:
READ IN APP

The biggest question in the world of tech right now is whether Jensen Huang will remain the CEO of Nvidia, perhaps the world’s most important company. Let’s hope he does. But the more interesting question is whether he can maintain his influence. Let’s hope he doesn’t. [...] The 63-year-old’s profile has taken a major hit over the last few days due to revelations that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a data center executive who U.S. officials believe is a Chinese spy. On Sunday, Jensen Huang acknowledged the affair and apologized, while Nvidia—saying it had no reason to believe national security had been compromised—pledged to launch an independent investigation. [...] Nvidia—whose stock fell 4.3 percent, or $192 billion, on Monday—has already said that Huang will remain CEO while the investigation is ongoing. That’s good. If Jensen Huang were to be ousted, the stakes could be enormous—not just for the company, but for the entire AI industry, not to mention the ongoing race between the U.S. and China for AI supremacy. Huang is the closest thing there is to Too Big to Fail, Personified.

Continue Reading The Free Press
